messages:
maria_pm: Quick sync — we need to prioritize which capability flags land for the public discovery endpoint before beta. Top asks: streaming support indicators, structured-output schemas, tool-calling compatibility, and per-model token limits. Who has capacity to spec tradeoffs this week?

jon_cs: Customers asking for explicit 'tools_supported' list so apps can render tool UIs without trial-and-error. Also need a flag for 'requires_auth_for_tools' (some models require HSM-backed tool calls).

ravi_ml: Agreed. From model side we can expose: streaming: boolean, streaming_chunk_granularity: (token|sentence|byte), structured_output: [json_schema_ids], tools: [{name, version, auth_required}], max_context_tokens, recommended_truncation_strategy.

maria_pm: That shape sounds sensible. Need to be conservative with field names and keep them stable for SDKs. Also add 'best_effort_warning' for structure outputs when model sometimes breaks schema.

dan_eng: Implementation notes: discovery endpoint needs to be cheap and cacheable. We shouldn't return large JSON schemas inline. Better to return stable schema ids and a separate /schemas/{id} endpoint. Caching TTL = 24h by default. Also streaming capabilities must indicate whether the model supports chunked SSE vs grpc streams.

sarah_sec: Important: any 'tools' entry that indicates 'auth_required' triggers an enterprise-only policy. We need metadata for required data retention and PII handling so compliance teams can decide. Suggest adding field 'data_retention: {logs: retention_days, kv_cache: retention_days}' — if that's too detailed for discovery, at least a pointer to a policy doc id.

maria_pm: Good point. Let's add 'policy_doc_id' on model metadata. Keep retention details behind enterprise-only expanded metadata.

ravi_ml: On token limits: we should publish both 'max_input_tokens' and 'max_total_tokens' and 'recommended_window' (for streaming KV cache heuristics). Some models have dynamic limits depending on quantization; we can include 'limit_variants': ["q8_0:8192","fp16:16384"] but maybe that's too noisy.

dan_eng: We can include 'limit_variants' as optional array, but SDKs should use 'effective_max' after we run compatibility check during client handshake. For the endpoint, simple numeric fields are best.

maria_pm: Launch criteria proposal: must have discovery v1 that includes streaming boolean + transport enum, structured_output IDs + schemas endpoint, tools list with auth flag, and explicit max_total_tokens. Beta blocked until intake-bot confirms at least 3 internal SDKs can parse it.

intake-bot: [auto] Spec checklist updated: discovery_v1_props added, schemas_endpoint added, sdk_parsing_tests required=3.

jon_cs: Customer ask — ability to toggle visibility of tool metadata per workspace. Not all customers want tool lists exposed to end users. We need a model visibility flag or workspace override.

sarah_sec: That ties to auth: discovery should return different payloads for unauthenticated vs workspace-scoped calls. Public call returns minimal flags (streaming, token limits), authenticated returns tools + policy_doc_id. Document this in API contract.

dan_eng: One more operational item: rolling changes. When we add a tool to a model, we must support canary rollout: discovery responses must be versioned (model_capabilities_version) and SDKs should detect mismatches and request confirmation. Add 'capabilities_version' string.

ravi_ml: Also include 'model_variant_compat' map to indicate when a streaming capability is present only on some variants. Example response snippet for discovery v1 (for discussion):

```
{
  "model": "redwood-rl-1",
  "capabilities_version": "2026-03-15-v1",
  "streaming": true,
  "streaming_transport": "sse",
  "structured_output_schema_ids": ["schema:json:invoice-v2"],
  "tools": [{"name":"browser","version":"1.2","auth_required":true}],
  "max_input_tokens": 8192,
  "max_total_tokens": 16384,
  "policy_doc_id": "policy-enterprise-42"
}
```

maria_pm: That example is perfect. Action items: dan -> draft API contract + caching/canary behavior. ravi -> list ML-driven edge cases (schema drift, partial streaming). sarah -> compliance pointer and workspace auth matrix. jon -> customer communication draft (what we expose public vs workspace). I'll own prioritization and triage for beta.

dan_eng: Timeline: I'll put a PR with the OpenAPI sketch by EOD Wednesday. Can we aim for internal SDK parsing tests by next Tue?

jon_cs: That works. I'll line up 2 pilot customers for tools visibility testing.

sarah_sec: FYI — any model flag that exposes tool names must go through security review checklist. I'll add to the backlog for this sprint.

maria_pm: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after dan's PR. If anything critical pops up, @here call it out. :+1:
